newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut hails U.S. court ruling on tobacco suit.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut hails U.S. court ruling on tobacco suit.

text.p: Connecticut Attorney General Richard Blumenthal Thursday hailed a federal court decision allowing the state to press ahead with a lawsuit to recover money spent to treat smoking-related illnesses.

Federal Judge Peter Dorsey on Monday dismissed a lawsuit filed by four tobacco companies seeking to block the state's suit, which also seeks to halt aggressive marketing of tobacco products to children and teenagers, Blumenthal said.
Blumenthal said it was the first time a federal judge has dismissed this type of tobacco industry action against a state.

He called the ruling a major win for Connecticut's effort to halt marketing of tobacco products to children and end other practices that have caused the state to spend hundreds of millions of dollars to pay for tobacco-related illnesses.

"This decision, which explicitly recognises the principle that the federal government should not interfere with legitimate state functions, clears the way for our case to continue," Blumenthal said in a statement.
"These four companies attempted to use the federal courts to pre-empt our lawsuit and their efforts have been resoundingly rejected," Blumenthal said.
The industry's suit was filed by Philip Morris Cos. Inc., the world's largest cigarette maker, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co., Brown & Williamson Tobacco Co., and Lorillard Tobacco.
Connecticut's suit against the companies and three related organisations alleges violations of the state's antitrust and unfair trade laws and other claims.
